skills.name: Attack position
skills.description: The ready stance for anything rough or fast: pedals level, weight on your feet, knees and elbows bent and out, hips back, eyes up.
skills.why: Every other skill starts from here. Bent limbs soak up hits, and weight in your feet keeps the tires gripping instead of your hands taking the bike for a ride.

drills.name: Parking-lot hover
drills.how: Roll slowly on flat ground, stand in attack position and hold it for 20 seconds. Check: pedals level, heels down, elbows out, chin over the stem. Repeat 5 times.

drills.name: Bump soak
drills.how: Roll over a curb or small bump in attack position and let your arms and legs absorb it so your head stays level. Do 10 passes.

drills.name: Trail switch
drills.how: On an easy descent, call out each time you switch from seated to attack position before a rough section. Aim to be set up before every rough bit, not in it.

skills.mastery_test: You've got it when you go into attack position without thinking before every rough or fast section of an easy trail, and your head stays level over small bumps.

media.caption: Attack position from the side and front

skills.name: Braking control
skills.description: Braking hard and early before a section, then letting off so the wheels roll through it. Mostly front brake, one finger, heels down.
skills.why: Controlled braking means you pick your speed before trouble instead of grabbing brakes in the middle of it, which is what washes out tires and starts most crashes.

drills.name: Stop-line
drills.how: Mark a line on a gentle slope. Ride at it at a steady speed and stop with your front wheel on it, using both brakes, without skidding. Do 10 stops, getting a little faster each time.

drills.name: Brake, release, roll
drills.how: Pick a corner or rough patch on an easy trail. Do all your braking before it, then let off completely and roll through. Repeat 5 runs.

drills.name: One-finger feel
drills.how: Ride a gentle descent using only one finger on each lever, adjusting speed smoothly with no skids. Notice how much the front brake can do.

skills.mastery_test: You've got it when you can stop on a line without skidding from moderate speed, and on an easy trail you're off the brakes through every corner and rough patch.

media.caption: Braking before a corner, rolling through it

skills.name: Looking ahead
skills.description: Keeping your eyes 3 to 5 seconds down the trail, on where you want to go, not on the rock right in front of your wheel.
skills.why: The bike goes where you look. Looking ahead gives your brain time to plan, smooths out your speed and keeps you off the obstacles you're scared of.

drills.name: Cone weave
drills.how: Set 5 markers in a loose line on flat ground. Weave through them looking at the marker after next, never the one you're passing.

drills.name: Call it
drills.how: On an easy trail, say out loud the next feature you see coming ("rock, left turn, roots"). If you can't name it before you're on it, look further.

drills.name: Exit spotting
drills.how: In every corner of a run, turn your head to the exit before you turn the bars. Count how many corners you remembered.

skills.mastery_test: You've got it when you can ride an easy trail you know while calling out features before you reach them, and you look through every corner to its exit.

media.caption: Head-cam: where your eyes should be

skills.name: Bike-body separation
skills.description: Letting the bike move underneath you while your body stays calm: the bike leans, tips and rises while your hips and head follow a smooth line.
skills.why: Cornering, steeps, drops and wheel lifts all ask the bike to move one way while you stay balanced. Riders who keep their body glued to the bike get thrown around by it.

drills.name: Figure eights
drills.how: Mark two cones 4 m apart on flat ground. Ride figure eights around them, leaning the bike under you while your chest stays upright and over the bottom bracket. 5 minutes.

drills.name: Push-pull
drills.how: Roll slowly in attack position and push the bike forward with straight arms, then pull it back to bent arms, without your hips moving. 10 reps a pass, 5 passes.

drills.name: Lean-only turns
drills.how: On a grassy slope, turn by leaning the bike only, keeping your shoulders level with the horizon. Do 10 turns each way.

skills.mastery_test: You've got it when you can ride tight figure eights with the bike leaned well over while your head stays above the bottom bracket, and push the bike out and back at walking speed without your hips moving.

media.caption: Bike leaning under a still rider

skills.name: Track stand
skills.description: Balancing on the bike at a standstill, pedals level, front wheel turned slightly, using small pedal and brake pressure to hold your spot.
skills.why: Balance at zero speed is what lets you pause on a tricky switchback, wait for a line to clear, or set up a move on a technical climb without putting a foot down.

drills.name: Uphill hold
drills.how: Face up a gentle slope, front wheel turned toward your lead foot. Hold your spot with light pedal pressure against the slope. Count your seconds; 10 tries.

drills.name: Brake-stand
drills.how: On flat ground, roll to a stop and balance on the brakes, rocking forward and back a few cm to stay up. 10 tries.

drills.name: Stop-go line
drills.how: Ride a line of 5 markers and stop for a 3-second stand at each one without dabbing.

skills.mastery_test: You've got it when you can hold a track stand for 15 seconds on flat ground and 10 seconds on a slope, either foot forward.

skills.name: Climbing position
skills.description: Staying seated and centred on steep climbs: elbows low, chest toward the bars, sliding forward on the saddle so the front stays down and the rear keeps grip.
skills.why: Most riders fail climbs because the front wheel lifts or the back wheel spins. The right position keeps both tyres working, so steep climbs become a matter of fitness rather than luck.

drills.name: Steepest-hill test
drills.how: Find a steep, smooth climb. Ride it seated, sliding forward and dropping your elbows as it steepens. Note how high you got; 5 tries.

drills.name: Front wheel check
drills.how: On a steep pitch, deliberately sit back until the front gets light, then move forward until it's planted. Feel the difference; 5 reps.

drills.name: Smooth spin
drills.how: Climb a loose section in an easy gear with a smooth, round pedal stroke, no surges. 5 runs without the rear spinning out.

skills.mastery_test: You've got it when you can climb a steep, loose fire-road pitch seated without the front lifting or the rear spinning out.

media.caption: Seated climbing position on a steep pitch

skills.name: Ratcheting
skills.description: Pedalling with partial strokes, back and forth, so a pedal never hits a rock or root while you keep moving.
skills.why: Full pedal strokes in rocky terrain mean pedal strikes, which stop you dead. Ratcheting keeps power going through tech, up and down.

drills.name: Quarter strokes
drills.how: On flat ground, move using only quarter strokes between 3 o'clock and 6 o'clock with your lead foot, back-pedalling between them. 3 lengths of a car park.

drills.name: Pedal-strike course
drills.how: Lay sticks across a gentle climb every metre. Ratchet through so your pedals stay clear of them. 5 runs.

drills.name: Rocky climb
drills.how: Pick a rocky climb you usually dab on. Ratchet through the rough part. 5 attempts.

skills.mastery_test: You've got it when you can climb a rocky section by ratcheting with no pedal strikes and no dabs.

media.caption: Ratcheting through rocks on a climb

skills.name: Climbing ledges
skills.description: Getting up a step on a climb: lift the front onto it, power stroke, then shift your weight forward to unweight and drive the rear wheel up.
skills.why: Ledges are what end most technical climbs. Getting both wheels up a step while keeping momentum is the key move for clean climbs.

drills.name: Curb ups
drills.how: Ride up a 10–15 cm curb from a slow roll: front lift, weight forward, rear up. 10 each side.

drills.name: Two-step
drills.how: Find two steps close together and climb both without stopping. 5 attempts.

drills.name: Slow-speed ledge
drills.how: Approach a trail ledge from a track stand, then go up it from almost zero speed. 5 attempts.

skills.mastery_test: You've got it when you can climb a 20 cm ledge on a trail climb without dabbing, 4 times out of 5.

media.caption: Front lift and rear unweight up a ledge

skills.name: Technical climbs
skills.description: Cleaning steep, rocky, rooty climbs by reading the line, picking where to put power down, and linking ledges, ratchets and kicks without stopping.
skills.why: Clean tech climbs mean you get to the top of the trail with energy left, and they show complete control at low speed, which most descents also need.

drills.name: Section repeats
drills.how: Pick the hardest 20 m of a tech climb and session it until you clean it. Log how many tries it took.

drills.name: No-dab climb
drills.how: Ride a whole technical climb aiming for zero dabs. Count your dabs and try to beat it.

drills.name: Line walk
drills.how: Walk a climb you can't clean and plan exactly where each wheel goes, then ride your plan.

skills.mastery_test: You've got it when you can clean a black-rated technical climb with no foot down.

media.caption: Linking ledges on a technical climb

skills.name: Flat corners
skills.description: Turning on flat or off-camber dirt: brake before, outside pedal down, weight into the outside foot and inside hand, lean the bike more than your body.
skills.why: Most trail corners have no berm. Getting grip on flat dirt is what lets you carry speed instead of skidding or stopping at every turn.

drills.name: Figure eights
drills.how: Ride figure eights around two markers on grass or dirt. Drop the outside pedal each turn and press the bike under you while your body stays upright. 5 minutes.

drills.name: Hand-heavy turns
drills.how: In a wide turn, push down on the inside grip and feel the front tire bite. Go a little faster each lap until the front starts to drift, then back off.

drills.name: Slow-in, fast-out
drills.how: On a trail corner, brake to a speed that feels too slow, then pedal out of the exit. Time 3 runs and try to make the exit faster each time.

skills.mastery_test: You've got it when you can ride a figure eight with the bike leaning under you and no skids, and take the flat corners on a green trail without touching the brakes mid-turn.

media.caption: Flat corner: bike lean vs body lean

skills.name: Berms
skills.description: Riding banked turns: enter high, look to the exit, stay square to the berm's surface and push into it to come out faster than you went in.
skills.why: Berms hand you free speed if you work them, and cost you speed if you brake in them. They're also the base for flow trails and jump lines.

drills.name: No-brake berm
drills.how: Pick one berm. Ride it 5 times, braking before the entry and never inside. Note your exit speed.

drills.name: Push the wall
drills.how: As you enter, sink into the berm with legs and arms, then extend out of it on the exit like you're pushing the bike into the wall. 5 runs.

drills.name: High line, low line
drills.how: Ride the same berm entering high and entering low. Feel which keeps more speed for you.

skills.mastery_test: You've got it when you can ride a berm without braking in it and come out at least as fast as you went in, every time on a run of 3 or more berms.

skills.name: Switchbacks
skills.description: Tight, steep hairpins: slow right down before, go wide on the entry, look all the way around, and turn late at the apex.
skills.why: Switchbacks are where riders dab and walk. Riding them clean saves energy on climbs and descents and is a big confidence step.

drills.name: Tight circles
drills.how: On flat ground, ride the tightest circle you can without a foot down, in both directions. Use a little rear brake and keep pedaling lightly.

drills.name: Wide entry
drills.how: On a switchback, ride the outside of the trail on the way in and only turn once you can see the exit. 5 tries.

drills.name: Head first
drills.how: Turn your head and shoulders all the way to the exit before the bike turns. Say "look" out loud as you do.

skills.mastery_test: You've got it when you can ride 3 switchbacks in a row on a blue trail, up or down, with no foot down.

skills.name: Loose corners
skills.description: Cornering on loose, dry or gravelly dirt: braking earlier, weighting the outside pedal and keeping your weight low and centred so the tyres can slide a little and still bite.
skills.why: Loose corners are where most washouts happen. Knowing how much the tyres can slide before they let go turns them from scary into fun.

drills.name: Gravel circles
drills.how: On loose gravel, ride circles that get tighter, pushing hard into the outside pedal. 5 minutes each way.

drills.name: Brake and release
drills.how: On a loose corner, brake hard on the straight before, then let go fully as you lean. 10 runs.

drills.name: Same corner, more speed
drills.how: Session one loose corner and enter 1 km/h faster each run until the tyres start to drift.

skills.mastery_test: You've got it when you can ride loose, dry corners at a steady speed without the front washing out, and recover a small rear slide without dabbing.

media.caption: Weighting the outside pedal on loose dirt

skills.name: Off-camber traverses
skills.description: Riding across slopes that tilt away: keeping the bike upright, your weight on the outside (downhill) pedal and your hips over the bike so the tyres don't slide downhill.
skills.why: Off-camber sections show up on every mountain, often with roots. Leaning into the slope like a corner is the instinct that makes riders slide out.

drills.name: Grass traverse
drills.how: Ride across a grassy slope with your downhill pedal down and the bike vertical. 10 passes each way.

drills.name: Off-camber roots
drills.how: Find a rooty off-camber section and ride it 5 times, keeping your weight centred and not braking on the roots.

drills.name: Look uphill
drills.how: On a traverse, keep your eyes on the exit and your hips level. 5 passes without the rear stepping out.

skills.mastery_test: You've got it when you can ride an off-camber, rooty section at trail speed without the wheels sliding downhill.

media.caption: Bike upright across an off-camber slope

skills.name: Nose pivots
skills.description: Turning on the front wheel: brake the front, let the rear lift, and swing it around so you can make switchbacks too tight to ride round.
skills.why: The tightest switchbacks on steep trails can't be ridden normally. A nose pivot lets you clean them instead of walking.

drills.name: Flat ground pivots
drills.how: From a slow roll, brake the front, lift the rear and move it 20–30 cm sideways. 10 each way.

drills.name: Quarter turns
drills.how: Build to swinging the rear a quarter turn before it lands. 10 each way.

drills.name: Tight switchback
drills.how: Session a tight switchback you usually walk, using a pivot halfway round. 10 attempts.

skills.mastery_test: You've got it when you can clean a switchback too tight to roll by pivoting the rear wheel around, both directions.

media.caption: Nose pivot on a tight switchback

skills.name: Controlled drifts
skills.description: Deliberately sliding the rear wheel into a corner to point the bike at the exit, then catching it with your weight on the outside pedal.
skills.why: Fast riders on loose trails slide on purpose. Steering the rear wheel lets you take sharper lines without losing speed.

drills.name: Brake slides
drills.how: On a loose flat area, brake the rear and steer to slide it 30 cm, then release. 10 each way.

drills.name: Slide and catch
drills.how: In a wide loose corner, start the slide at entry and catch it before the apex. 10 runs.

drills.name: Line choice
drills.how: Pick a corner and drift into the same exit line 5 times in a row.

skills.mastery_test: You've got it when you can start a rear-wheel drift going into a loose corner and come out on your chosen line, both directions.

skills.name: Wheel lift
skills.description: Lifting the front wheel by shifting your hips back and pushing the bars forward and up, not by yanking with your arms.
skills.why: Wheel lifts get the front over roots, rocks and edges instead of into them. They're the first step to manuals and bunny hops.

drills.name: Hip throw
drills.how: Rolling slowly, drop your chest, then push your hips back toward the rear axle with straight arms. The front should get light. 10 reps.

drills.name: Line hop
drills.how: Lift the front wheel over a line on the ground, then a stick, then a curb-height object. 10 of each.

drills.name: Root practice
drills.how: On a rooty section, lift the front over each root so only the back wheel hits it.

skills.mastery_test: You've got it when you can lift the front wheel over a curb-height obstacle while rolling, 5 times out of 5, using your hips and not your arms.

skills.name: Manual
skills.description: Rolling on the back wheel without pedaling, balanced with your hips low and back and arms straight, controlling height with the rear brake and your knees.
skills.why: Manuals carry you over holes, take the edge off drops and let you pump through terrain. They're a key ingredient for small drops and jumps.

drills.name: Find the balance point
drills.how: On a gentle slope, lift the front and hold it up as long as you can with straight arms, covering the rear brake. Use the brake to bring it down if you go too far. 15 tries.

drills.name: Distance markers
drills.how: Mark 1, 2 and 4 bike lengths on flat ground. Count how far each manual goes and log your best.

drills.name: Manual a dip
drills.how: Find a small dip or puddle. Manual over it so the front never drops in.

skills.mastery_test: You've got it when you can manual 3 bike lengths on flat ground, 3 times in a row, without pedaling.

skills.name: Stoppie
skills.description: Lifting the rear wheel by braking the front hard and pushing your hips forward, then setting it back down gently.
skills.why: Knowing how far you can load the front before going over the bars makes hard front braking safe, and it's the basis for nose pivots and placing the rear wheel.

drills.name: Tiny lifts
drills.how: Walk-speed rolls: brake the front sharply and let the rear come up a few cm. 15 reps.

drills.name: Hold it
drills.how: Build up to holding the rear in the air for a second before setting it down. 10 reps.

drills.name: Rear placement
drills.how: Lift the rear and set it down 10 cm to one side. 10 each way.

skills.mastery_test: You've got it when you can lift the rear 20 cm from a slow roll and set it down with control, 5 times in a row.

skills.name: Bunny hop
skills.description: Getting both wheels off the ground from a roll: manual the front up, then jump your feet and push the bars forward so the rear follows.
skills.why: Bunny hops clear logs, holes and rocks, let you change line in the air, and are how you pop off lips for jumps and drops.

drills.name: Two-part hop
drills.how: Practise front up (manual), then rear up (scoop the pedals and push the bars forward), as separate moves. 10 of each, then join them.

drills.name: Line to stick
drills.how: Hop a line on the ground, then a stick, then a low object. Only raise the height when both wheels clear 5 times.

drills.name: Trail hop
drills.how: On an easy trail, hop over 5 small roots or rocks instead of rolling them.

skills.mastery_test: You've got it when you can bunny hop a 15 cm (6 inch) object from a roll with both wheels clearing it, 4 times out of 5.

skills.name: Manualing rollers
skills.description: Manualing from the back of one roller over the next, landing the front on its backside so you keep speed instead of bumping up and down.
skills.why: Joining rollers with manuals is a big source of speed on flow trails and pump tracks, and it trains manual timing under pressure.

drills.name: Single roller
drills.how: Manual off the top of a roller and land the front on the backside of the next. 10 reps.

drills.name: Two in a row
drills.how: Link two manuals across three rollers. 10 runs.

drills.name: No pedals
drills.how: Ride a roller section without pedalling, only pumping and manualing. Count how many rollers you clear.

skills.mastery_test: You've got it when you can manual across two rollers in a row without the front touching down, 3 runs out of 5.

skills.name: Side hops
skills.description: Hopping both wheels sideways from a standstill or slow roll to move the bike onto a new line, over a rock or across a rut.
skills.why: Side hops get you out of ruts, around switchbacks and onto ledges where there's no run-up. They're the hardest test of hop power and balance.

drills.name: Line hops
drills.how: Side hop over a chalk line from a track stand. 10 each way.

drills.name: Height
drills.how: Side hop onto a 10 cm board, then 20 cm. 10 each way.

drills.name: Trail use
drills.how: Find a rut or rock and side hop out of it onto a better line. 10 attempts.

skills.mastery_test: You've got it when you can side hop 30 cm sideways onto a 20 cm step from a standstill, both directions.

skills.name: Pumping
skills.description: Gaining speed without pedaling by pushing the bike down into the backsides of bumps and letting it come up on the faces.
skills.why: Pumping is free speed and control. It's how you ride rollers, berms and jumps smoothly, and it teaches you to work with the ground instead of against it.

drills.name: Pump track laps
drills.how: Ride a pump track (or a run of small bumps) without pedaling. Count how far you get each lap.

drills.name: Push the backside
drills.how: On one roller, stay light on the way up, then push hard with arms and legs on the way down. 10 passes.

drills.name: No-pedal section
drills.how: Pick a short rolling bit of trail and ride it without pedaling, pumping every dip.

skills.mastery_test: You've got it when you can do a full lap of a pump track, or a run of 5 rollers, without pedaling and come out at the same speed or faster.

skills.name: Rollers
skills.description: Riding a series of smooth bumps by pumping each one, keeping both wheels on the ground and staying in control at speed.
skills.why: Rollers teach timing over lips. Staying low over them at speed is the step before jumping off them.

drills.name: Stay grounded
drills.how: Ride a roller section at medium speed and keep both wheels on the ground by soaking the lips with your legs. 5 runs.

drills.name: Faster each run
drills.how: Ride the same rollers 5 times, adding a little speed each time, still pumping instead of getting bucked.

drills.name: Speed check
drills.how: Ride rollers with no pedaling and see if you hold your entry speed to the end.

skills.mastery_test: You've got it when you can ride a set of rollers at speed with both wheels staying on the ground and without pedaling.

skills.name: Tabletops
skills.description: Jumping a lip with a flat top, so coming up short lands safely on the deck. Compress into the lip, extend off it, and land with both wheels together on the down ramp.
skills.why: Tabletops are where jumping starts. They're forgiving, so you can learn takeoff timing and speed without the risk of a gap.

drills.name: Roll it first
drills.how: Roll over the tabletop slowly, then at medium speed, to learn its shape before leaving the ground.

drills.name: Deck to down ramp
drills.how: Add speed one run at a time: land on the deck, then the edge, then the down ramp. 2 or 3 runs at each step.

drills.name: Compress and spring
drills.how: Push into the face of the lip with your legs, then let the bike come up under you. Don't pull up on the bars.

skills.mastery_test: You've got it when you can land on the down ramp of a small tabletop, with both wheels together and no casing, 5 times in a row.

skills.name: Gap jumps
skills.description: Jumping across an open gap between a takeoff and a landing, where coming up short means casing or going into the gap.
skills.why: Gaps are a big step in commitment and speed judgement. Riding them well opens up jump lines and bike parks.

drills.name: Speed match
drills.how: Find a tabletop the same length as the gap. Ride it at the speed that lands you on its down ramp, and note that speed (or the pedal strokes it takes).

drills.name: Watch and follow
drills.how: Watch a rider who clears the gap. Follow them in at their speed, with a safe distance between you.

drills.name: Commit check
drills.how: Before trying, roll the takeoff and landing on foot. Only go when your speed is the same as on the matched tabletop.

skills.mastery_test: You've got it when you can clear a small gap jump (1–2 m) and land on the down ramp, 5 times in a row.

media.caption: Gap jump: matching speed from a tabletop

skills.name: Hip jumps
skills.description: Jumps that change direction in the air: you turn the bike in the air and land on a landing angled away from the takeoff.
skills.why: Hips appear in every bike park and on many natural trails. They join turning and jumping, which is how fast riders link corners and features.

drills.name: Look and turn
drills.how: On a small tabletop, look over your shoulder toward a cone beside the landing as you take off. 10 each way.

drills.name: Small hip
drills.how: Ride a small hip jump, turning your hips and bars together in the air. 10 runs.

drills.name: Both ways
drills.how: Session a hip you can ride both ways (or two mirror hips). 5 each way.

skills.mastery_test: You've got it when you can clear a bike-park hip jump in both directions and land straight down the landing.

media.caption: Turning the bike in the air on a hip

skills.name: Step-ups and step-downs
skills.description: Jumps where the landing is higher (step-up) or lower (step-down) than the takeoff, which need a different pop and timing than a level tabletop.
skills.why: Natural trails are full of step-ups and step-downs. Judging speed when the landing isn't level is what lets you ride new jump lines on-sight.

drills.name: Step-up pop
drills.how: Ride a small step-up, pumping hard into the lip and pushing the bike up to the landing. 10 runs.

drills.name: Step-down float
drills.how: Ride a small step-down, staying relaxed and letting the bike float down to the landing. 10 runs.

drills.name: Speed check
drills.how: On each, find the slowest speed that still makes the landing. 5 runs each.

skills.mastery_test: You've got it when you can clear a step-up and a step-down on the trail, landing on the transition each time.

skills.name: Scrubs
skills.description: Tilting the bike over at the takeoff so you stay low over a jump instead of going high, keeping speed for what's next.
skills.why: Racers scrub because time in the air is slow time. Scrubs also let you ride jumps that kick you too high, with control.

drills.name: Tilt on a roller
drills.how: On a roller, push the bike down and to one side as it crests, keeping it close to the ground. 10 each way.

drills.name: Small table scrub
drills.how: Scrub a small tabletop, landing on the deck lower than a normal jump. 10 runs.

drills.name: Line scrub
drills.how: Scrub every jump on a short jump line. 5 runs, counting how many you scrub.

skills.mastery_test: You've got it when you can scrub a medium jump so you clearly stay lower than your normal jump and land smoothly.

skills.name: Whips
skills.description: Swinging the back of the bike out sideways in the air and bringing it straight again before you land.
skills.why: Whips are style, but they're also proof of complete control in the air: being able to move the bike around and still land straight.

drills.name: Pop and kick
drills.how: On a small tabletop, push the rear sideways with your hips just after takeoff. 10 runs.

drills.name: Bring it back
drills.how: Increase the whip each run, always landing straight. 10 runs.

drills.name: Both sides
drills.how: Try whipping your less natural way. 10 runs.

skills.mastery_test: You've got it when you can throw a clear whip on a medium jump and land straight and on line.

skills.name: Pro jump lines
skills.description: Riding a whole pro or double-black jump line top to bottom, linking big gaps and drops with no tabletop decks.
skills.why: Pro lines are the hardest test of speed control in the air: each jump sets up the next, and there's no room to fix a mistake.

drills.name: Section by section
drills.how: Session each jump of the line on its own until you clear it every time.

drills.name: Two in a row
drills.how: Link pairs of jumps at the speed the line needs. 5 runs per pair.

drills.name: Full line
drills.how: Ride the whole line top to bottom. Log each clean run.

skills.mastery_test: You've got it when you can ride a double-black or pro jump line top to bottom cleanly, 3 runs in a row.

skills.name: Roll-offs
skills.description: Rolling slowly off a small ledge with the wheels following the ground: hips back, arms extended to push the front down, then absorb the landing.
skills.why: Roll-offs teach you to manage the moment the front drops away. They're the safe way down most ledges and the first step to drops.

drills.name: Curb roll
drills.how: Roll off a curb slowly, pushing the front wheel down as it goes over and moving your hips back. 10 times.

drills.name: Push the bars
drills.how: At the edge, extend your arms to put the front wheel on the ground, then let the back wheel follow while you stay centred.

drills.name: Trail ledges
drills.how: Ride 3 small trail ledges at walking pace without braking on the edge.

skills.mastery_test: You've got it when you can roll off a 30 cm (1 foot) ledge at walking pace, staying centred with no nose-dive, 5 times in a row.

skills.name: Small drops
skills.description: Riding off a ledge at speed so both wheels land together: a small manual at the lip keeps the front up, then push the bike down to land.
skills.why: Above walking speed you can't roll off safely, because the front drops first. Dropping lets you ride ledges at trail speed without stopping.

drills.name: Manual the lip
drills.how: On a curb, ride at a moderate speed and do a small manual as the front wheel reaches the edge, so both wheels land together. 10 times.

drills.name: Land and absorb
drills.how: Aim to land both wheels at once and soak it up with your legs. Film one and check.

drills.name: Step up the height
drills.how: Move from a curb to a 40–60 cm drop only when the smaller one feels boring.

skills.mastery_test: You've got it when you can ride off a 50 cm (about 2 foot) drop at trail speed and land both wheels together, 5 times in a row.

skills.name: Big drops
skills.description: Drops over 1 m: matching speed to the landing, a confident pop or manual off the lip, and landing on a down slope with full-body absorption.
skills.why: Big drops are mostly speed judgement and commitment. Learning them properly is what keeps them from becoming a hospital trip.

drills.name: Landing check
drills.how: Before any drop, walk it. Find where the landing slopes down and the speed that puts you there.

drills.name: Ladder up
drills.how: Ride the next size up only after 5 clean landings on the current size.

drills.name: Follow a friend
drills.how: Follow a rider who's done the drop, at their speed.

skills.mastery_test: You've got it when you can ride a drop of 1 m or more to a down-sloping landing, landing both wheels together and in control, 3 times in a row.

media.caption: Big drop to a down slope

skills.name: Drops to flat
skills.description: Drops that land on flat ground instead of a slope: you need enough speed to land both wheels together and bent limbs to soak up the hit.
skills.why: Lots of trail drops land flat. Landing them nose-first or rear-first hurts; landing them flat is the hardest drop to do smoothly.

drills.name: Curb drops
drills.how: Roll off a 30 cm curb to flat at speed, landing both wheels at once. 10 runs.

drills.name: Absorb
drills.how: Land with deep knee and elbow bend, counting a soft 'one' as you land. 10 runs.

drills.name: Height ladder
drills.how: Move up to 60 cm, then 90 cm drops to flat once each feels easy. 5 runs at each height.

skills.mastery_test: You've got it when you can land a 90 cm drop to flat with both wheels together and no harsh bottom-out.

media.caption: Drop to flat, both wheels landing

skills.name: Big-mountain drops
skills.description: Drops of 2 m or more on natural terrain: steep run-ins, rough takeoffs and sloped or rocky landings you have to read on the day.
skills.why: Big natural drops are where real skill shows: there's no shaped lip, so judging speed, takeoff and landing is entirely up to you.

drills.name: Scout first
drills.how: Walk every big drop before you ride it: run-in, takeoff, landing and run-out. Plan your speed.

drills.name: Step up the height
drills.how: Session 1.5 m, then 2 m natural drops, 5 runs each, before going bigger.

drills.name: Natural landing
drills.how: Ride drops onto a rough or rocky landing, picking the smooth spot. 5 runs.

skills.mastery_test: You've got it when you can ride a 2 m natural drop on a double-black trail with control on the landing.

skills.name: Roots and rocks
skills.description: Rolling over loose rocks and wet or slippery roots: loose arms, weight in the feet, light on the bars, and crossing roots as straight as you can.
skills.why: Roots and rocks are on nearly every trail. Riding them relaxed instead of tense stops them throwing you off line.

drills.name: Straight across
drills.how: Find an angled root. Ride it 5 times, adjusting your line so you cross it as close to straight on as you can.

drills.name: Light hands
drills.how: Ride a rooty section with a looser grip than feels normal, letting the bike move under you.

drills.name: Momentum run
drills.how: Ride the same rocky section 3 times, a little faster each time. Speed often makes it smoother.

skills.mastery_test: You've got it when you can ride a rooty or rocky section on a blue trail with no foot down and no line changes you didn't choose.

skills.name: Rock gardens
skills.description: Riding a long, dense section of rocks: pick a line before you enter, carry steady speed, lift the front over square edges and keep looking ahead.
skills.why: Rock gardens punish hesitation. Line choice and steady momentum make them flow instead of turning into a stop-and-dab.

drills.name: Walk the line
drills.how: Walk the rock garden first. Pick a line and name 3 key rocks you'll aim for.

drills.name: Sections
drills.how: Ride the garden in parts: top third, then two thirds, then all of it.

drills.name: Same line, more speed
drills.how: Ride the same line 3 times, each a bit faster, keeping off the brakes inside it.

skills.mastery_test: You've got it when you can ride a whole rock garden on a blue or black trail with no foot down, on the line you picked, 3 runs in a row.

media.caption: Picking a line through a rock garden

skills.name: Steep rolls
skills.description: Riding steep rollers and chutes: hips back and low, arms extended, smooth braking without locking up, and eyes on the run-out.
skills.why: Steeps are a head game as much as a skill. Good body position and brake control let you ride lines that used to mean getting off and walking.

drills.name: Look at the run-out
drills.how: Stand at the top of a steep roll and pick the spot where it flattens out. Keep your eyes there the whole way down.

drills.name: Feather, don't lock
drills.how: Ride a moderate steep, braking with steady pressure and no skids. If the rear locks, ease off.

drills.name: Steeper step
drills.how: Find 3 steep rolls of increasing angle and ride each until it's calm.

skills.mastery_test: You've got it when you can ride a steep roll on a black trail with no skids and in control at the bottom, 3 times in a row.

media.caption: Body position on a steep roll

skills.name: Pedal kicks
skills.description: A sharp half pedal stroke combined with a pull on the bike that pops the rear wheel over a rock or root that would otherwise stop it.
skills.why: Pedal kicks keep the bike moving in tech where speed is low, both climbing and descending. They're how you clean the sections where everyone else hikes.

drills.name: Stick kicks
drills.how: Lay a log on flat ground. Roll at walking pace and kick to get the rear over it. 10 reps.

drills.name: Rocky climb kicks
drills.how: On a rocky climb, kick the rear over the biggest rock. 10 attempts.

drills.name: Tech descent kicks
drills.how: On a slow, rocky descent, kick over a rock to keep momentum. 10 attempts.

skills.mastery_test: You've got it when you can use a pedal kick to get the rear wheel over a 15 cm rock from walking pace, 4 times out of 5.

skills.name: Steeps
skills.description: Long, steep chutes where you have to control speed all the way down: heels down, hips back but not behind the saddle, braking in short bursts so the tyres don't lock.
skills.why: Steeps feel scariest of all, but control on them makes big mountain trails possible. Skidding on a steep means losing control.

drills.name: Brake-release-brake
drills.how: On a steep slope, brake for 1 second, release for 1, repeat, keeping the tyres rolling. 5 runs.

drills.name: Elbows out
drills.how: On a steep run-in, check: arms bent, chest low, heels down. 5 runs.

drills.name: Stop on a steep
drills.how: Stop halfway down a steep without skidding, then roll on. 5 runs.

skills.mastery_test: You've got it when you can ride a steep chute on a black trail with control, stopping on it if you choose, without the wheels locking.

media.caption: Controlling speed on a steep chute

skills.name: Rock ledges
skills.description: Drops off rock ledges in the middle of a technical section, where you need to pick the takeoff, place the front wheel and keep control for what comes after.
skills.why: Natural ledges aren't clean, shaped drops; they're inside chunk. Getting off them smoothly is what keeps rough trails flowing.

drills.name: Ledge inspection
drills.how: Walk a ledge: find your takeoff and landing spot. Then ride it 5 times on that line.

drills.name: Manual off
drills.how: Manual the front off a small ledge so the wheels land together. 10 runs.

drills.name: Ledge into rocks
drills.how: Ride a ledge that lands into more rocks, staying off the brakes on the landing. 5 runs.

skills.mastery_test: You've got it when you can ride a 50 cm rock ledge in a rock garden with both wheels landing smoothly and keep going without stopping.

media.caption: Ledge drop in a rock garden

skills.name: Wet roots
skills.description: Riding over slick, wet roots without sliding: crossing them as square as possible, staying off the brakes and keeping your weight centred and light.
skills.why: Wet roots are the slipperiest thing on a trail. Riders who can ride them stay upright year-round.

drills.name: Square across
drills.how: Find wet roots on a flat trail. Steer so you cross each one as square as you can. 10 passes.

drills.name: No-brake roots
drills.how: Brake before the roots, then roll over them with no brakes. 10 passes.

drills.name: Light hop
drills.how: Unweight the bike as you cross diagonal roots. 10 passes.

skills.mastery_test: You've got it when you can ride a wet, rooty section of a blue trail without the wheels sliding out or putting a foot down.

skills.name: High-speed chunk
skills.description: Riding rough rock and root sections at full speed: staying light, pumping off the backsides, letting the bike move and picking lines several features ahead.
skills.why: At speed the bike skims across rough ground rather than dropping into every hole. It's the defining skill of an expert descender.

drills.name: Same section, faster
drills.how: Session a rock garden 5 times, going faster each run while staying in control.

drills.name: Look further
drills.how: Ride a chunky section looking at the exit, not the rocks in front of you. 5 runs.

drills.name: Pump the backsides
drills.how: Push into the backside of rocks to gain speed. 5 runs.

skills.mastery_test: You've got it when you can ride a double-black rocky section at full speed without braking in the middle of it.

skills.name: Line choice
skills.description: Reading a trail to pick the fastest, smoothest or safest line, and committing to it, including lines that aren't the obvious one.
skills.why: The same skills go further on a better line. Picking lines is how riders go faster without taking more risk.

drills.name: Three lines
drills.how: Pick a section and ride it on three different lines. Note which was smoothest and fastest.

drills.name: Call it
drills.how: Before a section, say your line out loud, then ride it exactly. 10 sections.

drills.name: Follow a faster rider
drills.how: Follow a faster rider and copy their lines on a trail you know.

skills.mastery_test: You've got it when you can ride a trail you know on a planned line and explain why each part of it is faster or smoother than the obvious line.

media.caption: Reading the line on a trail

skills.name: Pumping for speed
skills.description: Making speed with no pedalling: pumping rollers, berms and the backsides of rocks so the bike accelerates.
skills.why: On a flow trail or pump track, pumping is faster than pedalling. It's free speed and a sign that you're working with the terrain.

drills.name: Pump track laps
drills.how: Ride laps of a pump track without pedalling. Count laps before you lose speed.

drills.name: Berm exit push
drills.how: Push down out of each berm on a flow trail to accelerate. 5 runs.

drills.name: No-pedal descent
drills.how: Ride a flow trail without pedalling and try to beat your time with pedalling.

skills.mastery_test: You've got it when you can ride 2 laps of a pump track without pedalling, finishing faster than you started.

skills.name: Braking zones
skills.description: Braking hard in the right spots and nowhere else: short, strong stops in smooth sections before corners and features, then riding everything else off the brakes.
skills.why: Fast riders don't brake less, they brake better. Moving all your braking to the right places saves seconds and keeps tyres gripping where it matters.

drills.name: Mark your zones
drills.how: On a trail you know, pick one braking spot before each corner. Ride it braking only there. 5 runs.

drills.name: Late braking
drills.how: Move each zone a bike-length later every run until it's too late, then back off one. 5 runs.

drills.name: Timed runs
drills.how: Time a section with your normal braking and with planned zones. Compare.

skills.mastery_test: You've got it when you can ride a trail you know braking only in planned zones, and it's faster than when you brake as you go.

skills.name: Riding on-sight
skills.description: Riding a trail you've never seen at a good pace: reading it as it comes, setting speed for blind sections and staying ready for surprises.
skills.why: Every new trail, trip and race is ridden on-sight. It's the skill that turns practice on home trails into riding anywhere.

drills.name: New trail, steady pace
drills.how: Ride a trail you've never ridden at a steady, controlled pace, looking as far ahead as you can.

drills.name: Blind crests
drills.how: Slow down for every blind crest and corner, then speed up once you see the exit.

drills.name: Second run
drills.how: Ride the new trail again, faster, and note what you'd missed.

skills.mastery_test: You've got it when you can ride a black trail you've never seen at a good pace without stopping to look at sections first.

skills.name: Race pace
skills.description: Linking everything on a full descent at your fastest controlled pace: lines, braking zones, pumping, jumps and corners, start to finish.
skills.why: Holding race pace for a whole trail is the ultimate speed test. Mistakes add up, so it rewards consistency as much as speed.

drills.name: Timed laps
drills.how: Time 3 laps of the same descent, using the app's trail times. Aim for your 3 runs within 3% of each other.

drills.name: Section splits
drills.how: Split a trail into 3 sections and work on the slowest one.

drills.name: Race day
drills.how: Enter a local enduro or downhill race, or time a run against a friend.

skills.mastery_test: You've got it when you can set a PR on a black trail and match it within 3% on your next run.

skills.name: MTB Master
skills.description: The final skill: riding the hardest trails on the mountain with everything you've learnt, clean, fast and in control.
skills.why: Mastering every branch means you can ride anything. This test puts it all together on one run.

drills.name: Plan a master line
drills.how: Choose a double-black trail that includes steeps, drops, tech and jumps. Walk or ride it slowly first.

drills.name: Section it
drills.how: Session each hard section until you clean it every time.

drills.name: Full send
drills.how: Ride the trail top to bottom at pace, with no dabs and no stops.

skills.mastery_test: You've got it when you can ride a double-black trail top to bottom, clean, at race pace, including its drops, jumps and tech.

media.caption: A master run, top to bottom
